name: theme-media-references-feedback-3
body:
source: review theme-library-refs/feedback-3 (target requirements.requirement.theme-media-references). Spine gap: the requirement drove domain.entity.theme, domain.value.media-asset, domain.service.load-template-library and domain.service.template-registry, but the serve-time half of the capability — the rewrite of theme CSS (theme route) and of `.css` served from the `media/` route to the resolved library's served URLs — traced to no domain node realised by solution.component.http-server. The three new implemented-by anchors for this change (rewriteThemeCSS, themeFileHandler, mediaFileHandler) sit on http-server, so the serve-time half had no requirement → domain → http-server → code path.

Query evidence (not the reviewer's example taken on trust): `MATCH (d)-[:RealisedBy]->(s {fqn:'solution.component.http-server'})` returns domain.entity.deck-rebuilt, domain.entity.template-library, domain.service.serve-deck, domain.service.watch-deck. Of these, domain.entity.template-library is the genuinely driven one: the requirement's references resolve inside the resolved library (its own theme directory, the shared `media/` tree, another theme) and are rewritten to the library-served URLs, and the sibling requirement template-media — the same serve-time library-asset serving concern — already drives domain.entity.template-library.

Resolution [autonomous]: added the minimal edge `requirements.requirement.theme-media-references --drives--> domain.entity.template-library`, giving the serve-time half the path requirement → template-library → http-server → the three code anchors. No existing drives edge was removed (all four remain correct). domain.service.serve-deck was not added: its body scopes it to the deck page/error page, embedded assets, deck assets/, the /templates gallery and live reload, not the resolved library's media/theme routes, so a drives edge there would over-connect.
